about.label: About
about.headline: I write the frontend. If the product needs more, I do that too.
about.p1: Most days I work on Razaan, the admin system at Melal Bank. Screens first. When something is missing — an API route, Docker, logs, a session store — I pick that up as well.
about.p2: I started in support and CRM. That is still useful. I have seen where people drop a form, so I try to keep the UI ordinary and clear.

projects.label: Work
projects.title: Selected work
projects.subtitle: Razaan first, then the apps next to it. The last card is smaller GitHub work.

razean.title: Razaan — CoreOffice
razean.description: Razaan is the bank's centralized admin system — finance, HR, projects, assets, and the modules around them. I worked on several of those modules, not the whole product.
story: Goods and assets. Parts of HR, including evaluation. Documents, grouping, announcements.
Messages and notifications with SignalR / WebSocket.
A relationship graph for entities — any record to any record, and how they depend on each other.

portal.title: Razaan Portal
portal.description: A side app next to Razaan. Easier access for day-to-day files: treasury payslips, transparency uploads, collections, payroll. The data goes into Razaan and the process starts there.
story: Sits between the bank and Razaan.
Transparency, collections, and payroll modules.
An upload in the portal creates the matching process in Razaan.

loan.title: VAMA — loan requests
loan.description: A public site for loan requests (started with marriage and childbirth; other types can be added). Applicants upload documents online. The request becomes a Razaan process at their branch. The branch checks the file, asks for missing pieces, then they come in.
story: Public forms land in a Razaan cartable at the chosen branch.
Next.js BFF in front of the main backend — our API routes.
User tokens in Redis. The usual public-site checks (OWASP).

monitoring.title: VAMA monitoring
monitoring.description: For the public loan app we needed our own picture — users, errors, and whether the app is up. We dockerized VAMA and put Elasticsearch, Graylog, Grafana, and Prometheus on it.
story: Logs: errors and where people get stuck.
Grafana for CPU, RAM, memory.
Nginx in front. Fail2Ban if a client hits the box too hard.

workflow.title: Razaan workflows (BPMN)
workflow.description: In Razaan, requests go through a workflow — support, banking, welfare, and so on. Another team builds the Camunda and Form.io definitions. We read the APIs, render the forms, show the flow, and give each person a cartable.
story: Cartable: what is on your desk, who had it, where it goes next.
Custom Form.io components on our side — dates and a few others.
The BPMN flow is shown next to the request.

migration.title: New Razaan — new stack
migration.description: This is the new version of Razaan on a new tech stack. The old app was CRA. We rebuilt it with Next.js and Turborepo: CoreOffice, Storybook, and Docusaurus.
story: Three apps in one repo: the ERP, Storybook, and the docs.
App Router, our own BFF (API routes), React Query instead of Redux Saga for server data.
Our own tokens in CSS Modules. Look is still close to Ant Design so we can add another theme later if we need to.

minis.title: Smaller things
minis.description: Practice and side work — not a seventh product. The crypto dashboard and the emotion chatbot both have live demos.
story: Crypto rates dashboard — React Query, i18n, the first structured frontend I finished.
LLM chatbot with sentiment analysis — thesis work. Live demo; repo is private.
A document generator I used to try Docusaurus. A todo list. The usual practice apps.

melal.summary: Razaan and the apps around it: modules in the ERP, the portal, VAMA, the entity graph, the cartable, the new stack, and monitoring on our BFF.
highlights: Razaan modules — assets, HR evaluation, documents, announcements, realtime messages
Portal for treasury / transparency / collections / payroll files
VAMA (vama.melalbank.ir) — public forms into Razaan cartables
BPMN cartable — we render Form.io + Camunda, another team authors the processes
Turborepo rewrite + Prometheus / Grafana / Graylog on the BFF

iapps_intern.summary: First engineering seat. A lot of Coursera. Small campaign work (Yalda, Nowruz). Then the new iApps stack on Turborepo — PWA, developer panel, backoffice. I spent most of my time on the backoffice. It was a learning job, and that is fine.
highlights: Backoffice on the new Turborepo (PWA + dev panel + backoffice together)
React Hook Form, Redux, MUI, i18n
Crypto dashboard on the side while I learned React Query

iapps_crm.summary: Didar CRM. I ran support, mapped B2B/B2C journeys, and sat between the business and the people who built the product.
highlights: Customer journeys — what people actually do, not what the ticket says

iapps_support.summary: Tickets, QC, writing down how things were supposed to work. This is where I learned that a screen can be 'done' and still fail in the field.
highlights: Process notes the next person could actually use
